body: Euclidean projection onto sum x_i=1 is invariant under one uniform shift of its argument: expanding squared distance changes the objective by a constant on the feasible set. Thus the global unknown h is irrelevant to this operation and was not learned. Component Lipschitz envelopes enclose every valid source; nonexpansive projection and contraction bound the response perturbation by E/m, then the residual inequality gives the displayed certificate. Signed/nonsymmetric K is allowed if a valid induced-norm upper bound yields q<1; the source uses an outward Frobenius bound. Noisy envelopes remain outer, even if H is not one globally compatible source. On the257-point mesh, the halfwidth is a-Lipschitz so add a/512 before the36bit outward norm bound.
